newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast prods up with NYMEX amid quiet talk.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast prods up with NYMEX amid quiet talk.

text.p: U.S. West Coast wholesale gasoline prices got a lift from the futures market Monday while local supply and demand remained stable, traders said.
NYMEX gasoline settled up 1.08 cents at 61.96 cents a gallon Monday, just below the intraday high of 62.10 cents.

Traders talked Los Angeles CARB unleaded gasoline 1.50 cents a gallon higher from Friday to 73/74 cents, with deals reported at 73 and 73.50 cents. Conventional unleaded rose 1.50 cents to 66.50/67.50 cents a gallon.
Conventional low sulphur in L.A. also climbed, tracking a 0.80 cent-rise in heating oil futures in New York.
"EPA" diesel stood one cent higher than Friday at 63/64 cents.
West Coast gas stocks remained tight, at 26.9 million, or 2.3 million barrels below a year ago, according to weekly reports published by the industry and government.
Refineries continued to ramp up from planned maintenance, with higher output reflected in last week's 91 percent plant capacity figure, a 1.2 percentage point from the week before.
